## Closing thesis and next-session catalysts

**Own conditional analysis:** the equity rebound is constructive, but QQQ sits at a falling 50-day average and below its 20-day average while IWM remains below its 50-day. A higher close alone does not confirm a durable breakout. Prioritize a confirmed break/retest or rejection; do not sell a range before the post-data opening range stabilizes.

The [Federal Reserve statement](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20261028a.htm), released October 28 at 14:00 ET, kept the target at 3.75–4.00%. Two voters preferred a quarter-point increase. That leaves inflation/rates sensitivity relevant to technology and small caps.

The [BEA calendar](https://www.bea.gov/news/schedule) schedules both advance Q3 GDP and September personal income/outlays (including PCE) for **Thursday October 29 at 08:30 ET**. The [NYSE calendar](https://www.nyse.com/markets/hours-calendars) shows October 29 as a regular session, 09:30–16:00 ET. Amazon's [official announcement](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/company-news/amazon-earnings-q3-2026-report) sets its earnings call at **17:00 ET October 29**; carrying Friday ETF spreads overnight introduces that event. Microsoft/Alphabet post-close results can reset technology levels: refresh the actual overnight tape before entry; Wednesday close is a baseline, not the next opening price.

### Technical map: daily bars through October 28

Saved public Yahoo daily OHLC, retrieved October 28 approximately 16:26 ET. Session bars carry 09:30 timestamps identifying the daily bar; the coverage here is the completed cash session. Calculated simple averages use daily closes, not intraday bars. Index points for SPX; USD/share for ETFs.

| Instrument | Close | Session low / high | SMA20 / SMA50 / SMA200 | Prior-session low / high |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| SPX | 7743.98 | 7718.37 / 7758.43 | 7734.34 / 7698.05 / 7302.71 | 7677.16 / 7736.24 |
| QQQ | 725.61 | 720.30 / 726.12 | 732.48 / 725.42 / 678.72 | 713.59 / 722.87 |
| IWM | 281.36 | 279.05 / 281.47 | 277.27 / 285.00 / 278.53 | 276.89 / 280.40 |

SPX's 7,734 SMA20/7,736 prior high cluster is the first support test, then 7,718 and 7,698 SMA50. Above 7,758, the 20-session high 7,845 is the next broader reference. QQQ needs to hold 725.42 SMA50 and clear 726.12 before attacking 732.48 SMA20; 720.30 and 713.59 are failure references. IWM's 281.47 high is the immediate trigger, with 284.64 recent high/285.00 SMA50 overhead; 279.05 and 278.53 SMA200 mark support.

**Cross-asset scenarios:** saved TLT closed 80.99, down 0.78%, below the prior 81.47 low; its falling 200-day average is 84.69. That weakens a simple “lower yields support everything” thesis. VIX fell to 16.93 from 17.52, but this is a 30-day SPX volatility index, not next-day ETF implied volatility. If hot inflation lifts yields and TLT cannot reclaim 81.47, favor confirmed QQQ downside rather than buying an unconfirmed equity dip. If inflation is benign and TLT reclaims its prior range while equities hold support, bullish call/put-spread alternatives gain confirmation. Mixed cross-assets or failed breakouts mean no trade.

### Latest few days and post-close update

Independent source research as of **October 28, 23:35 ET**: [SPX history](https://www.investing.com/indices/us-spx-500-historical-data) places the October 21 high at 7,770.40, October 27 low at 7,677.16 and October 26 high at 7,702.13. The 7,758–7,770 zone is therefore recent resistance, not a breakout already achieved. Rejection followed by loss of 7,718 points toward 7,702/7,677; sustained acceptance above 7,770 invalidates that bearish scenario.

[QQQ history and extended-hours snapshot](https://stockanalysis.com/etf/qqq/history/) reports **718.05 at 19:59 ET October 28**, versus the 725.61 cash close. That post-close gap puts the old 720.30 low overhead: a failed reclaim of 720.3–722.9 is more relevant than blindly waiting for a fresh break from above. October 21 high was 727.95; October 22 selloff volume approximately 64.6 million versus about 30–33 million during the recovery supports caution, not proof of future selling. [Microsoft's issuer release](https://news.microsoft.com/source/2026/10/28/microsoft-announces-first-quarter-results-2/) reports revenue growth and strong Azure growth; [Reuters' Alphabet report](https://new.streetinsider.com/Reuters/Alphabet%2Bshares%2Bfall%2Bafter%2Brevenue%2Bmiss%2C%2Bcash%2Bburn%2Bworsens/27249195.html) describes disappointing revenue/cash flow and a sharp after-hours share decline. Tech dispersion can overwhelm the prior cash-close pattern. The QQQ snapshot is delayed historical context, not a live Thursday quote.

[IWM daily history](https://stockanalysis.com/etf/iwm/history/) reports recent closes 275.75 → 276.99 → 280.18 → 281.29, showing relative rebound strength; hold 280.4 and accept above 281.5 to target the 284.2–284.6 zone, while loss of approximately 279.1 invalidates. Its reported 281.29 close differs from saved Yahoo's 281.36; avoid false precision and use rounded zones.

[TLT history](https://stockanalysis.com/etf/tlt/history/) shows 80.99 close and 80.73 low, with failed 81.73–81.92 base. Failed reclaim of 81.27–81.47 followed by loss of 80.73 would confirm rate pressure; reclaim 81.76–81.92 undermines it. [GLD history](https://ca.investing.com/etfs/spdr-gold-trust-historical-data) shows 373.51 close versus 366.61 October 23 and 378.95 October 21: watch resistance 373.6–373.9, then 376.2/379.6; support 368.4–368.9. These are cross-asset checks, not extra positions.

Also watch **08:30 ET weekly claims** on the [Labor Department archive](https://oui.doleta.gov/unemploy/archive.asp) and the October 29 seven-year auction date on the [Treasury tentative schedule](https://home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/TentativeAuctionScheduleQ22026.pdf); auction time was not independently verified here. Amazon's 17:00 call is after Thursday 0DTE expiry, rather than an intraday earnings release. No verified Apple event is assumed. Mixed macro/technology dispersion supports a condor only after a stable opening range and actual premium check, never simply because the Fed meeting ended.
